title: Top Ext consequence of normalized derived Koszul adjunction
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $i:U\hookrightarrow P$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] into an open $P$ of $\mathbf A^n_S$. Let $0\leq c\leq n$ and suppose its ideal $I$ is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of length $c$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], with $C=I/I^2$ locally free of rank $c$. Put $V=i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$ and $D_i=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV$, where $\vee=\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O_U)$, using [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_P$-modules
$$i_*D_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Ext^c_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})$$
for the sheaf Ext of [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext]. It is the inverse of $H^c(\rho_i)$ for the normalized derived Koszul comparison $\rho_i$ of [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] applied to $U\to S$ with $d=n-c$. Thus its normalization is specified, and it is independent of generators and ambient-line trivializations and compatible with open restriction.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext): degree-c consequence of the derived isomorphism in lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison.

proof.text: Apply the unconditional part of [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] with $X=U$, $f:U\to S$ the composite, $d=n-c$, and the one-chart cover consisting of $U$ itself. The inequalities give $d\geq0$ and $c=n-d$; the closed immersion, polynomial ambient open, Koszul regularity and conormal rank are exactly its hypotheses. It supplies the specified isomorphism $\rho_i:R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})\xrightarrow{\sim}(i_*D_i)[-c]$. Only its unconditional assertion is used: no existence theorem for a relative dualizing object and no flatness or Noetherian assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext): passage from the normalized derived comparison to degree-c sheaf Ext.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext], the degree-$c$ cohomology of the source of $\rho_i$ is precisely $\mathcal Ext^c_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S})$. On the target, represent $i_*D_i$ by the complex concentrated in degree zero. The shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] places $(i_*D_i)[-c]$ in degree $c$, with all differentials zero. Thus its degree-$c$ cohomology is canonically $\ker(0:i_*D_i\to0)/\operatorname{im}(0:0\to i_*D_i)=i_*D_i$, by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The cohomology functor sends the two inverse identities for $\rho_i$ to inverse identities, so $H^c(\rho_i)$ is an isomorphism from the displayed Ext sheaf to $i_*D_i$. Take its inverse to obtain the asserted arrow.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext): passage from the normalized derived comparison to degree-c sheaf Ext.

proof.text: The normalization is exactly $(H^c(\rho_i))^{-1}$ by construction, so no further choice of sign or basis is made. The independence of generators and ambient-line frames in [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] is equality of its derived comparisons; applying the cohomology functor preserves these equalities, and taking inverses preserves them too. For an open $W\subseteq P$, restricting the formula $\ker d^c/\operatorname{im}d^{c-1}$ of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives the same cohomology formula on $W$: kernels and the locally represented images and quotients have the same local sections after restriction. Apply this to the open-restriction compatibility of $\rho_i$ supplied by the comparison node. Its degree-$c$ map restricts to the corresponding map on $W$, and its inverse does as well. This proves all asserted compatibilities.
